title: Fast On-device LLM Inference with NPUs (llm.npu)
technique: mobile NPU offloading of prefill via fixed-size prompt chunks with shared graphs, outlier extraction to CPU/GPU, out-of-order block scheduling across NPU and CPU/GPU

optimized_metrics.evidence: The primary design goal of llm.npu is to reduce the prefill latency and energy consumption.
The primary design goal of llm.npu is to reduce the prefill latency and energy consumption.
significantly and consistently outperforms all baselines in terms of prefill latency and energy consumption while preserving inference accuracy (<1% loss compared to FP16).

headline_claim.text: llm.npu achieves 22.4× faster prefill speed and 30.7× energy savings on average, and up to 32.8× speedup in an end-to-end real-world application. For the first time, llm.npu achieves more than 1,000 tokens/sec prefilling for a billion-sized model.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 12-14 prefill latency/speed at prompt lengths 64/256/1024
end-to-end latency on UI automation, chat summary, etc.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We mainly measure LLM inference accuracy, prefill latency, prefill energy consumption, prefill memory consumption and end-to-end inference latency.
metric_definitions.notes: prefill-phase only; single request on device; no queueing; speed in tokens/sec = prompt tokens / prefill time (not formally defined)

load_regime: single request on-device, batch=1, prompt lengths 64/256/1024; repeated runs (three times) on datasets
tradeoff_acknowledged: decoding is not accelerated (uses CPU backend); NPU needs outlier handling to maintain accuracy
workloads: LongBench, DroidTask UI automation, chat summarization, email auto-reply
extractor_notes: Not a serving paper; prefill latency is the stated target, closest canonical code TTFT but TTFT is never named. Thought: could be OTHER:prefill_latency. Energy is a co-objective.
